notes: Side-by-side text (docs/archive/engine/fidelity/11-WPB-side-by-side.md). Counts follow 01-MASTER-BRIEF.md §11 as
amended by WP-B: a text element is a maximal run of consecutive, vertically stacked, horizontally
overlapping in-flow sibling blocks and anonymous inline runs, whose content is inline-only, under one
parent, with no intervening non-text sibling; each block or run is one paragraph; atomic inline boxes
with their own horizontal geometry are elements of their own.
So a flex or grid row splits into one element per item (kv, kv-loose, dl, unit, contents), a flex
column whose items stack stays one element (kpi, stacked-right, the badge's txt), a padded chip leaves
its paragraph whatever the spaces around it (chip-tail, chip-mid, chips-only) while an unpadded style
change stays a run (styled-word), and an anonymous run beside an icon, a swatch or an image hugs its
own lines (pills, legend, icon-inline). Alignment and anchor are derived from the line boxes: kpi,
badge and the centred cases come out 'center' (and 'middle' where a flex or grid box centres them
vertically), stacked-right 'right'.
Shapes: kv 4 (panel fill + 3 row borders), kv-loose 1 (border), kpi 1, badge 3 (item fill, its left
border, the badge circle), pills 4 (2 fills + 2 dots), chip-tail 1, chip-mid 1, chips-only 2, legend 3,
contents 4 (the two cells inside display:contents are painted too), centred 2, swatch-li 2,
swatch-inline 1, padded-inline 1 — every chip painted once, by the element walk.
The seven cases at the bottom are the B1 critique's (fidelity-reports/b1-review.md), each pinning the rule
that answered it: chip-centre-wrap and chip-right-end (#2: a part-line after or before a chip that the
paragraph's alignment cannot place is a paragraph of its own), tight-pair (#8: STACK_TOL 0.15 — a 5 px pull
into the heading's line box is two elements), mark-around-chip (#3: the mark paints under the chip, the chip
reads between the texts), inline-flex-gap (#6: an inline-flex laying two items out is a layout), wrap-tags
(#9: a wrapped flex line is a row, not a stack) and li-chips (#11: a chips-only item keeps its bullet, on
the first chip's text). Shapes: chip-centre-wrap 1, chip-right-end 1, mark-around-chip 2, wrap-tags 3,
li-chips 2.
The eight cases after them are r1a's (plan 16 #25): a gap an inline box's margin or padding, or an empty inline box,
leaves between two texts of one line is carried by a space sized to it (its advance + letter spacing = the gap,
written as spc), so seam-bullet, seam-label, seam-formula, seam-legend, seam-unit, seam-centred and seam-wrap are one
text each with no glued-runs diagnostic and padded-inline's spaces carry its padding; faded is an in-flow text block
(on faded-card's fill) whose own opacity is on its text (run alpha) and the box it detaches (element opacity).
Counts by the amended 11: +10 text (7 seam cases, faded's 3), +3 shapes (seam-legend's 2 swatches, faded-card's fill).
Line counts were measured in Edge with the master's theme fonts forced (Calibri / Calibri Light);
a different theme font re-breaks them, the element and paragraph counts are structural and do not move.
